# Tarot Journal

A Skill Harbor house build for people who draw cards, and for the honestly curious. Tarot Journal does not predict anything, and it says so in its first line. The cards and their meanings are tradition, presented as tradition: all 78 cards are included, the 22 major arcana and the 56 minor arcana in their four suits, each with concise traditional keywords for upright and, where the tradition gives them, reversed. What the skill adds is the part readings usually skip: it keeps score, with you, over time, and it writes the draw down before anyone interprets it.

It starts by asking what you believe. Sceptical but curious, occasional, or a serious practitioner? You pick your rhythm, a card of the day, a weekly draw, or both; your format, 1 card or 3 cards; and your reading style, upright only or upright and reversed. You can draw from your own deck and dictate the cards, or let the assistant simulate a draw at random, labelled as simulated in the journal. Every draw goes into a folder that stays on your device: date, your question in your own words, the cards exactly as drawn, and only then the traditional lens.

Later, at the review, the assistant reads the entries back and asks for your verdict on each draw: resonated, did not resonate, or in between. Months later it can count from your own journal: which cards keep coming back, and how your verdicts split, always with the denominator visible, as observations about your notes and never as proof of anything. Free to use under...
